current.text: He is a projected starter for Toronto next to Quickley, Leonard, Barnes and Poeltl, and he is in the expected closing five.
He should start and play 30 or more minutes.
Toronto traded Brandon Ingram away and added Kawhi Leonard.
He loses usage to Kawhi Leonard and will have the ball less, which adds to his efficiency concerns.
Kawhi Leonard's load management helps him. He should step up on the nights Kawhi sits.
Sean expects his finishing next to Kawhi and Scottie Barnes to reach impressive levels this season.
Because of his contract situation, he could become a trade candidate if the season starts badly.
In category leagues he ranks outside the top 130. Picks around 90 to 107 are called too early.
Josh is very okay drafting him around pick 120.
Toronto is projected to win 52 games, or 56 to 57 if Kawhi plays 75 games.
Toronto is not deep beyond a solid top seven.
Toronto has 15 back-to-backs, with three of them in the fantasy playoffs.

durable.text: He is mainly a scorer with low defensive stats and lower efficiency.
He is worth clearly more in points leagues than in category leagues.
His FT% is a clear weakness on real volume and hurts a team's FT%.
He has limitations, especially on defense.

note: Barrett is priced as a last-roster-spot player: about 1 to 2 USD on Yahoo and ESPN, ranked 134 to 139, and he went for 1 USD in our league last season. That price fits a starter who plays 30 minutes and scores about 18 to 20 points. He is a points-league player, though. His 68.7% FT% hurts in our format, and his steals and blocks are low, so do not pay above 1 to 2 USD. Early in the season, check how much of the ball he gets next to Kawhi and how he produces on Kawhi's rest nights. Also keep in mind that Toronto has three back-to-backs during our playoffs.
